mainTopic: The exiles' sin offerings in עזרא (a community never dies; a הוראת שעה), and the אשכולות who ended with יוסף בן יועזר
overview: The גמרא brings a ברייתא quoting a פסוק in עזרא: the exiles returning from בבל brought twelve goats as sin offerings for the עבודה זרה done in the days of צדקיהו. Since the sinners from צדקיהו's time seem to have died, this challenges the view that a communal חטאת can be left to die (מתה). רב פפא answers that even that view agrees a communal חטאת whose owners died is still brought, because a community never dies, and the גמרא proves this from the goat offerings of יום טוב and ראש חודש, bought with half-shekel money. A second answer says many of the old sinners were still alive, as the פסוקים in עזרא about the loud crying show. The גמרא then asks how a חטאת could be brought for sins done on purpose, and רבי יוחנן answers that it was a הוראת שעה, supported by the extra sheep in the list. A new topic follows: the אשכולות, complete leaders who learned תורה like משה רבינו, ended with יוסף בן יועזר. The גמרא defends this against the 3,000 forgotten הלכות and the majority votes after משה. Finally, a story about a חסיד who lived long after יוסף בן יועזר and had no sin except keeping a goat challenges the ברייתא that later leaders had a flaw; the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא about the exiles' offerings in עזרא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא in which רבי יוסי quotes the פסוק about the offerings brought by the exiles returning from בבל, including twelve goats as sin offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: In the same way, רבי יוסי said: 'Those who came from the captivity, the children of the exile, brought burnt offerings: twelve bulls, ninety-nine rams, seventy-seven lambs, twelve goats as sin offerings. All of it was a burnt offering to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא quoting a פסוק in עזרא. This sets up a challenge that the גמרא will spell out a few steps later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word והתניא ('but isn't it taught') tells us a challenge is coming. The important detail is the twelve goats brought as sin offerings, which are communal חטאות. The גמרא will first clear up a question about the פסוק, and only then explain the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The children of the exile, the Jews returning from בבל
A burnt offering, burned completely on the מזבח and not eaten

steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not stated yet. Do not look for it in this step; the גמרא spells it out at קא סלקא דעתין.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתַנְיָא: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a ברייתא: Similarly, Rabbi Yosei said:
"Those who came from the captivity, the children of the exile,
brought burnt offerings...
twelve bulls...
ninety-nine rams,
phrases.notes: The פסוק itself in עזרא says ninety-six (תשעים וששה).

phrases.english: seventy-seven lambs,
twelve goats as sin offerings —
all of it was a burnt offering to the Lord."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתַנְיָא: כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source against the view in the earlier discussion that a communal חטאת can be left to die.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a communal חטאת whose owners already got atonement is left to die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Set up here. The full attack comes in step 5: these sin offerings were brought even though their owners had died.

steps.title: How can a חטאת be called an עולה?
steps.stepSummary: Before using the פסוק, the גמרא asks how the פסוק can say a sin offering was a burnt offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can a sin offering be brought as a burnt offering?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask about the wording of the פסוק. It says 'all was an עולה', yet a חטאת is a completely different kind of offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת and an עולה have different rules. The פסוק seems to lump them together. The גמרא needs to explain this before it can use the פסוק as a proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really brought? (a surprised question)

phrases.english: But can a sin offering be brought as a burnt offering?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the פסוק that was just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the פסוק mean when it calls the sin offerings an עולה?

steps.title: Like an עולה, these sin offerings were not eaten
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the sin offerings were 'like an עולה' in one way: they were not eaten. רבי יוסי says they were brought for עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It means 'like an עולה.' Just as an עולה is not eaten, so too this חטאת was not eaten. For רבי יוסי used to say: They brought them for the sin of עבודה זרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The פסוק does not mean the goats became real burnt offerings. It means they were treated like burnt offerings because no one ate them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most sin offerings are eaten by the כהנים. These goats were brought for עבודה זרה, and a sin offering of that kind is not eaten. That is why the פסוק can compare them to an עולה.

phrases.english: Rava said: like a burnt offering,
just as a burnt offering is not eaten,
so too, the sin offering was not eaten,
for Rabbi Yosei would say:
They brought them for idol worship,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the wording of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sin offerings were 'like an עולה' only in that they were not eaten, since they were brought for עבודה זרה.

steps.title: The sin was from the days of צדקיהו
steps.stepSummary: שמואל tells us which עבודה זרה these offerings were for: the idol worship done in the days of צדקיהו, during the time of the first בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: It was for the עבודה זרה that they did in the days of צדקיהו.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל adds a key fact: the sin these goats atoned for happened long before, in the days of צדקיהו. This fact sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: צדקיהו was the last king before the first בית המקדש was destroyed. The exiles came back generations later. So the גמרא assumes, for now, that the people who actually committed the sin were already dead when the offerings were brought. A later answer will question this.

keyTerms.meaning: In the days of King צדקיהו, the last king of יהודה before the destruction

steps.whyThisMatters: This time gap is the whole basis of the challenge. The owners of the חטאת had died, yet the offering was still brought.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: עַל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה שֶׁעָשׂוּ בִּימֵי צִדְקִיָּהוּ.
phrases.english: for the idol worship that they did in the days of Zedekiah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to רבי יוסי's statement: exactly which sin of עבודה זרה it was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exiles' sin offerings atoned for the עבודה זרה done in the days of צדקיהו.

steps.title: The owners had died, yet the חטאת was brought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out its challenge. It assumes that whoever holds a communal חטאת is left to die once its owners got atonement also holds the same when its owners died. Yet here the owners had died, and the offering was brought anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: We are assuming: whoever holds that a communal חטאת whose owners already got atonement is left to die also holds that a communal חטאת whose owners died is left to die. But here is a case where the owners died, and it was still brought!
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא explains why it brought the ברייתא. It is a challenge against the view that a communal חטאת can be left to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes the two cases go together: owners who got atonement and owners who died. But in the days of עזרא, the sinners from צדקיהו's time were dead, and their communal חטאת was still brought. So a communal חטאת whose owners died is not left to die, and the same should be true when its owners already got atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: It enters our mind, we are assuming
Whose owners already got atonement (through a different animal)
Is left to die; it is not offered

steps.confusionAlert: 'מתה' here does not mean the animal already died. It means the הלכה is to lock it away until it dies on its own, without offering it.

phrases.english: It enters our mind (we assume),
that the one who holds
that a communal sin offering whose owners got atonement is left to die,
also holds
that a communal sin offering whose owners died is left to die,
but here is a case where its owners died,
phrases.notes: The people who sinned in צדקיהו's days were long gone by the time of עזרא.

phrases.english: and it was still brought!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתִּין, לְמַאן דְּאִית לֵיהּ חַטַּאת צִבּוּר שֶׁנִּתְכַּפְּרוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא from step 1 and uses the time gap from step 4 to build the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a communal חטאת whose owners got atonement is left to die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that view also kills a communal חטאת whose owners died, then the exiles' offerings, whose owners were dead, should not have been brought. But they were.

steps.title: A community never dies
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that the two cases are different. Even the view that kills a communal חטאת whose owners got atonement agrees that one whose owners died is offered, because a community never dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Even the one who says a communal חטאת whose owners got atonement is left to die agrees that a communal חטאת whose owners died is not left to die, because a community does not die.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends the view under attack. He shows that the two cases do not go together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended on treating 'owners got atonement' and 'owners died' the same way. רב פפא says the owner of a communal offering is the community as a whole, and the community lives on even when its members die. So the exiles' offerings tell us nothing about a case where the owners already got atonement.

keyTerms.meaning: The community does not die; it continues on as one group

steps.whatToRemember: Even according to the view that a communal חטאת whose owners got atonement is left to die, a communal חטאת whose owners died is still offered, because a צבור never dies.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a basic rule about communal offerings: the community as a whole is the owner, so the death of individual members does not end its offering.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Even according to the one who said
that a communal sin offering whose owners got atonement is left to die,

phrases.aramaic: חַטַּאת צִבּוּר שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ אֵינָהּ מֵתָה,
phrases.english: a communal sin offering whose owners died is not left to die,
because the community does not die.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: אֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5 by showing that its assumption is wrong.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two cases: owners who got atonement versus owners who died
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought that whoever kills a communal חטאת whose owners got atonement would also kill one whose owners died.
steps.terutzMaskana: A communal חטאת whose owners died is offered according to everyone, because the community never dies. So the ברייתא is no proof against the other view.

steps.title: What is רב פפא's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רב פפא learns that a community never dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where does רב פפא know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source backs up רב פפא's rule that a community never dies. This question sets up the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6, רב פפא said a communal חטאת whose owners died is still brought, because a community never dies. He gave no source for this, so the גמרא now looks for one.

keyTerms.meaning: From where does he know it? A request for a source

phrases.english: From where does רב פפא know this?
phrases.notes: 'This' means his rule from step 6: a community never dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the answer רב פפא gave in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for the rule that a community never dies.

steps.title: The פסוק about sons replacing fathers is rejected as the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the פסוק 'Your sons shall be instead of your fathers' as the source. It rejects this, because the פסוק would then apply to a single person too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say the source is the פסוק 'Your sons shall be instead of your fathers.' But if so, the same should be true even for a single person!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out one possible source and then pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק suggests that sons take their fathers' place, as if the fathers were still alive. But the פסוק says nothing that limits it to a community. That would mean a son could bring his dead father's private חטאת, and we know that is not the הלכה. So this פסוק cannot be the source.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: introduces a problem with what was just said
A single person, as opposed to the community

phrases.english: If we say it is because it is written:
"Your sons shall be instead of your fathers,"
if so, then even a single person as well!
phrases.notes: He means a son could then bring the private חטאת of his father who died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to step 7's question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the פסוק in תהלים as the source for 'a community never dies.'
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק proves too much. Nothing in it limits it to a community, so it would let individuals bring offerings for their dead fathers.

steps.title: Proof from the goat offerings of יום טוב and ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: The real source is the communal goat offerings. The תורה says to buy them with money from the Temple collection, even though some of the people who gave that money may have died. This shows that a community never dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the reason that the community does not die: it comes from the goats of the festivals and of ראש חודש. The תורה says to bring them from the Temple collection chamber. But maybe the owners of these coins have died? So we must learn from this that the community does not die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real source for רב פפא's rule. It uses a case everyone knows: the communal goat sin offerings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goats brought on יום טוב and ראש חודש are חטאות. They are bought with the half-shekel money everyone gave earlier in the year. Some of those givers surely died before the offering was brought, yet the offering is still brought for the whole community. This only makes sense if a community, as a group, never dies.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat sin offerings brought for the community on יום טוב and ראש חודש
The money collected from the yearly half-shekels and kept in a chamber of the Temple, used to buy communal offerings
The Merciful One, meaning the תורה
Learn from this: a conclusion drawn from what was just said

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the idea that a communal offering belongs to the community as a group, not to a list of particular people.

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason
that the community does not die:
from the goats of the festivals and of ראש חודש,
as the Merciful One said:
Bring them from the Temple collection chamber.
But maybe the owners of these coins have died?
Rather, isn't it so? Learn from this
that the community does not die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the source rejected in step 8 with a working proof.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's rule that a community never dies.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The communal goat sin offerings are bought with coins from the Temple collection, even though some of the people who gave those coins have surely died.

steps.title: Second answer: the offerings were for people still alive
steps.stepSummary: A different answer to step 5's challenge: the sin offerings in עזרא's time were brought for people who were still alive. Many people who had seen the first בית המקדש were there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say instead: when they brought these sin offerings, they brought them for living people. As it is written: 'And many of the כהנים, the לויים, and the heads of the families, the old men who had seen the first House standing on its foundation, this House... were crying in a loud voice, and many shouted for joy.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a whole new answer to the challenge from step 5. This answer does not need the rule that a community never dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 asked how they could bring a חטאת whose owners had died. This answer says the owners had not died. Many people from the days of צדקיהו were still alive when the second בית המקדש was built, as the פסוק in עזרא shows.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say: introduces another possible answer

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
when they brought these sin offerings,
they brought them for living people, as it is written:
"And many of the כהנים, the לויים,
and the heads of the families, the old men
who had seen the first House
standing on its foundation, this House...
phrases.notes: The '...' skips part of the פסוק: 'when this House was before their eyes.'

phrases.english: were crying in a loud voice,
and many shouted for joy."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to step 5's challenge and gives a second answer, instead of רב פפא's answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the facts of the case: the owners were alive, so there is no question.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The offerings were brought for people who had already died.
steps.terutzMaskana: The offerings were brought for people who had sinned in צדקיהו's time and were still alive.

steps.title: Maybe the survivors were only a minority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second answer: maybe the people still alive were only a small minority.
steps.simpleTranslation: But maybe those people were a minority?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A communal sin offering is brought for a sin of the community, not of a few people. If only a few of the sinners were still alive, each one should have brought a private offering. So the fact that they brought communal offerings suggests they were still bringing them for people who had died.

keyTerms.meaning: A minority, a small part of the group

phrases.english: But maybe those people were a minority?
phrases.notes: 'Those' are the old people from the פסוק who had seen the first בית המקדש.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the second answer given in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 10 that the sin offerings were brought for living people.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the survivors were only a few, a communal offering would not fit them. So the offering must have been for the whole group, including people who had died.

steps.title: The criers were not a minority
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from the next פסוק: the crying was so loud that it could not be told apart from the shouts of joy. So the criers were many.
steps.simpleTranslation: You cannot say that, as it is written: 'And the people could not tell the sound of the joyful shouting from the sound of the people's crying.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the challenge from step 11 with the very next פסוק in עזרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the criers were only a few, their crying would have been drowned out by the joyful crowd. The פסוק says the two sounds could not be told apart, so the crying group was large. That means many of the sinners from צדקיהו's time were still alive, and step 10's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: You cannot say that: rejects the suggestion just made
A loud shout, here a shout of joy

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to how a sin offering could be brought for owners who had died. (1) רב פפא says a community never dies, which is proven from the goat offerings bought with half-shekel money. (2) The owners had not died: many of the sinners from צדקיהו's time were still alive, as shown in עזרא ג:יב-יג.

phrases.english: You cannot say that,
as it is written: "And the people could not tell the sound of the shouting
of joy from the sound of the people's crying."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 and keeps step 10's answer standing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A proof from a פסוק that removes the doubt.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe only a few of the old sinners were still alive.
steps.terutzMaskana: The crying was as loud as the joyful shouting, so the survivors were many.

steps.title: How could they bring sin offerings for sins done on purpose?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the sin offerings brought in עזרא's time: the people worshipped idols on purpose, and a חטאת is only for an accidental sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: How could they bring these offerings? They sinned on purpose!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the offerings brought by those who returned with עזרא. Those people had worshipped idols on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about whether the people were still alive. Now the גמרא attacks from a different side. A חטאת only atones for a sin done by mistake, but these were מזידין, people who sinned knowingly. So how could any sin offering be brought for them?

phrases.english: But how could they bring them as offerings?
phrases.notes: "Them" means the sin offerings brought in עזרא's time (עזרא 8:35).

phrases.english: After all, they were people who sinned on purpose!
phrases.notes: A sin offering only works for a sin done by mistake, so this seems not to fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהֵיכִי מַקְרְבִי לְהוּ? וַהֲרֵי מְזִידִין הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving the people were still alive, the גמרא raises a new problem with the same offerings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sin offerings brought for idol worship in עזרא's time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A חטאת is only for an accidental sin, and these people sinned on purpose.

steps.title: It was a one-time emergency ruling
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that these offerings were a הוראת שעה, a special ruling for that moment only.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: It was a ruling for that time only.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the challenge. The normal rule was set aside for that special moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן agrees that normally you cannot bring a חטאת for a sin done on purpose. But this was a הוראת שעה, a ruling made just for that special time. So the normal rule stays the same, and this case was an exception.

keyTerms.meaning: a ruling for that time only, a one-time emergency ruling

steps.confusionAlert: This does not change the rule. Sin offerings are still only for accidental sins; the offerings in עזרא's time were a one-time exception.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
It was a ruling for that time only.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הוֹרָאַת שָׁעָה הָיְתָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Special exception for one time (הוראת שעה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: These offerings must have followed the normal rules of a חטאת, which do not allow offerings for sins done on purpose.
steps.terutzMaskana: They were a one-time emergency ruling, so the normal rule did not apply.

steps.title: The sheep prove it was a special ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבי יוחנן: the bulls and goats match the twelve tribes, but the sheep match nothing in the normal rules, so this must have been a special ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense. Otherwise: the bulls and goats are fine, since they match the twelve tribes. But what do the sheep match? So it must have been a ruling for that time only.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for רבי יוחנן's answer from the list of offerings itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the normal rules, the bulls and goats can be explained as one for each of the twelve tribes. But the sheep in that list have no source in the normal rules at all. Since the sheep cannot be explained normally, the whole set of offerings must have been a הוראת שעה.

keyTerms.meaning: this also makes sense (the גמרא is giving support)
it is fine, it makes sense

steps.whatToRemember: The offerings in עזרא's time were a הוראת שעה. Proof: the sheep cannot be explained by the normal rules.

phrases.english: This also makes sense,
because if you do not say this —
it is fine with the bulls and goats,
since they match the twelve tribes,
phrases.notes: The פסוק lists twelve bulls and twelve goats, one for each tribe.

phrases.english: but what do the sheep match?
Rather, it was a ruling for that time only.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי מִסְתַּבְּרָא, דְּאִי לָא תֵּימָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי יוחנן's answer in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's claim that the offerings were a הוראת שעה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The sheep listed among the offerings, which match nothing in the normal rules

steps.title: The אשכולות ended with the two יוסף's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: once יוסף בן יועזר and יוסף בן יוחנן died, the אשכולות came to an end.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: when יוסף בן יועזר of צרידה and יוסף בן יוחנן of ירושלים died, the אשכולות ended.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a משנה from another place (סוטה 47a). This sets up the next steps, which explain the word אשכולות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a special kind of leader, called אשכולות, stopped existing after these two sages died. It does not yet explain what an אשכול is; the next step does that.

keyTerms.meaning: literally clusters (like clusters of grapes); a name for great leaders

phrases.english: We learned in a משנה there:

phrases.aramaic: מִשֶּׁמֵּת יוֹסֵף בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
phrases.english: From when Yosef ben Yoezer of Tzereida died
and Yosef ben Yochanan of Jerusalem,
the clusters came to an end.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic; the discussion of עזרא's offerings is finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After these two sages died, there were no more אשכולות.

steps.title: What an אשכול means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the word אשכולות: a person who has everything in him.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man who has everything in him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the hard word from the משנה. The question "what does it mean?" is not written; it is understood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אשכולות is read as if it were אִישׁ שֶׁהַכֹּל בּוֹ, "a man who has everything in him." So an אשכול is a complete person, full in every way, like a full cluster of grapes.

keyTerms.meaning: a man who has everything in him

phrases.english: A man who has everything in him.
phrases.notes: The sounds of אשכול are being read as אִישׁ שֶׁהַכֹּל, "a man who has it all."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the key word of the משנה in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the word אשכולות mean? (The question is understood, not written.)
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person who has everything in him.

steps.title: Until יוסף בן יועזר, leaders learned like משה רבינו
steps.stepSummary: שמואל teaches that all the אשכולות from משה until יוסף בן יועזר learned תורה like משה רבינו, and after that no one did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: All the אשכולות who led Israel from the days of משה until יוסף בן יועזר died learned תורה like משה רבינו. From then on, they did not learn תורה like משה רבינו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a teaching from שמואל about the same אשכולות. He tells us what was special about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said the אשכולות ended. שמואל adds what made them special: they learned תורה the way משה רבינו did. After יוסף בן יועזר died, the leaders no longer learned that way.

keyTerms.meaning: who stood up as leaders for Israel
learned Torah the way משה רבינו did

steps.whatToRemember: The אשכולות were complete leaders who learned תורה like משה רבינו. That level ended when יוסף בן יועזר died.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
All the clusters who stood as leaders for Israel

phrases.aramaic: מִימוֹת מֹשֶׁה עַד שֶׁמֵּת יוֹסֵף בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר —
phrases.english: from the days of Moshe until Yosef ben Yoezer died —
would learn Torah like Moshe our teacher,
from then on —

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיוּ לְמֵדִין תּוֹרָה כְּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ.
phrases.english: they did not learn Torah like Moshe our teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: כׇּל אֶשְׁכּוֹלוֹת שֶׁעָמְדוּ לָהֶן לְיִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another teaching about the אשכולות of step 16, telling us what made them special.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Until יוסף בן יועזר died, the leaders learned Torah like משה רבינו; after that, they did not.

steps.title: Three thousand הלכות were forgotten after משה died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל's claim from step 18 using another teaching of שמואל: 3,000 הלכות were forgotten during the mourning for משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב יהודה say in the name of שמואל: 3,000 הלכות were forgotten during the days of mourning for משה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question against step 18. If so much Torah was lost right after משה died, how can שמואל say the later sages learned just like him?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 claimed that the generations after משה learned תורה exactly the way he did. But losing 3,000 הלכות suggests their learning was already weaker. Both teachings come from שמואל, so they seem to contradict each other.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Yehuda say in the name of Shmuel:
Three thousand halachos were forgotten
during the days of mourning for Moshe!
phrases.notes: The point is: if that much was lost right after משה, how could the next sages learn just like him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's statement in step 18 with another statement from שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the אשכולות after משה learned Torah like משה רבינו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 3,000 הלכות were forgotten right after משה's death, the next generation's learning could not have matched his.

steps.title: What they forgot was lost, but what they knew they learned like משה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the forgotten הלכות were lost, but the הלכות they still knew were learned with the clarity of משה רבינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ones they forgot were forgotten, but the ones they knew, they learned like משה רבינו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 19 by separating the forgotten material from what was still known.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount of תורה went down, but the quality of their learning did not. שמואל's claim in step 18 is about how they learned, not about how much they knew. So the two teachings do not contradict each other.

phrases.english: Those that they forgot were forgotten,
but those that they did know,
they learned like Moshe our teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: the amount of Torah versus the quality of learning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forgetting 3,000 הלכות shows that their learning was weaker than משה's.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the amount was reduced. What remained was learned like משה.

steps.title: After משה, questions were decided by majority vote
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again with a ברייתא: after משה died, questions of טומאה and טהרה were decided by majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't it taught: from when משה died, if most said 'impure,' they declared it impure, and if most said 'pure,' they declared it pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to step 18, this time from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Deciding by majority means the sages disagreed and were not sure. That does not sound like learning with the full clarity of משה. So it seems their learning really did fall below his level.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים not included in the משנה
Pure; here, those who rule it pure (טהור)

phrases.english: But isn't it taught in a baraita:
From when Moshe died,
if those declaring it impure were the majority, they declared it impure,
and if those declaring it pure were the majority, they declared it pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 20 answered the first challenge, this brings a new challenge from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the later sages learned like משה רבינו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Needing a majority vote shows doubt and disagreement, which goes against the idea of learning with the clarity of משה.

steps.title: Majority vote applied only where understanding had shrunk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that majority vote was used only for the forgotten areas. What they still knew, they learned like משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where understanding had shrunk, they needed a majority. But what they did learn, they learned like משה רבינו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the ברייתא from step 21 by limiting the majority vote to the forgotten הלכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds on the answer in step 20. In the areas that were forgotten, the sages lacked a clear tradition, so they had to vote. Everything they still had was learned with משה's clarity.

phrases.english: Where the heart was reduced,
phrases.notes: He means: majority vote from the ברייתא was only for the forgotten הלכות, where understanding had become smaller.

phrases.english: but what they learned, they learned
like Moshe our teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 using the distinction from step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope: majority vote applied only to the forgotten material.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Majority voting shows that all their learning had dropped below משה's level.
steps.terutzMaskana: Majority vote was only for what was forgotten. Everything else was learned like משה.
steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's claim holds: after משה there was less תורה, but what remained was learned with his clarity. Majority votes were needed only for the forgotten parts.

steps.title: The אשכולות until יוסף בן יועזר had no flaw
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the אשכולות from משה until the death of יוסף בן יועזר had no flaw at all, but after that they had some flaw.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: all the אשכולות who led Israel from the days of משה until יוסף בן יועזר of צרידה died had no flaw in them. From then on, there was some flaw in them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that matches שמואל's teaching in step 18 and marks יוסף בן יועזר's death as the turning point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like step 18, this ברייתא draws a line at יוסף בן יועזר. Before him, the leaders were complete and without flaw. After him, some flaw appeared, which fits the end of the אשכולות mentioned in the משנה in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא, a teaching of the תנאים outside the משנה
Clusters; great leaders who had everything in them

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
All the clusters (great leaders) who stood for Israel
from the days of Moshe until the death of
Yosef ben Yoezer, the man of Tzereida,
had no flaw at all in them;
from then on,
there was some flaw in them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending שמואל in steps 19-22, the גמרא brings a ברייתא with a matching teaching about the אשכולות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The leaders from משה until יוסף בן יועזר had no flaw. After him, they had some flaw.
steps.whatToRemember: The death of יוסף בן יועזר is the turning point: it ended the flawless אשכולות who learned like משה.

steps.title: A sick pious man is given a goat for its milk
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a challenge with a ברייתא about a חסיד with heart pain. The doctors told him to drink warm milk every morning, so a goat was tied to his bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: there was a story with a certain pious man who suffered from pain in his heart. They asked the doctors, who said: his only cure is to suck warm milk every morning. So they brought a goat, tied it to the legs of his bed, and he would suck milk from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against step 23 by telling a story from a ברייתא. This step sets up the story; the actual challenge becomes clear at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only learn the background: a righteous man, a medical need, and a goat kept in his house. The goat is the key detail. The next steps will show that keeping it was his one sin.

keyTerms.meaning: A pious person who goes beyond the basic requirements
Groaning from pain in his heart

phrases.english: But isn't it taught: there was an incident with a certain pious man
who was groaning because of his heart,
and they asked the doctors, and they said:
there is no remedy for him
unless he sucks warm milk in the morning,
so they brought a goat and tied it for him
to the legs of his bed,
and he would suck milk from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a challenge against the claim in step 23 that the sages after יוסף בן יועזר had a flaw.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא in step 23 saying the אשכולות after יוסף בן יועזר had some flaw.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story will show a later sage with no sin except one minor matter, so later sages could also be flawless.

steps.title: His friends find only one sin: the goat
steps.stepSummary: The man's friends see the goat and call it an armed robber. They check his deeds and find no sin except the goat.
steps.simpleTranslation: The next day his friends came to visit him. When they saw the goat they said: there is an armed robber in his house, and we are coming in to visit him?! They sat and examined his deeds and found no sin in him except that goat alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The man's friends look into his deeds and find that his only sin is the goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This builds the challenge: an outside check shows the man was almost perfect, with only one sin. That makes him a strong example of a sage with no real flaw.

phrases.english: The next day his friends came in to visit him.
When they saw the goat, they said:
An armed robber is inside his house,
phrases.notes: They mean the goat. Goats eat from other people's fields, so it is like a robber in the house.

phrases.english: and we are coming in to visit him?!
They sat and examined his deeds,
and they found no sin in him
except the sin of that goat alone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story and shows the man had only one sin.
steps.raayaObject: That this חסיד was free of sin except for the goat.
steps.raayaSupportSource: His friends' examination of his deeds in the ברייתא.

steps.title: The man himself confirms the goat was his only sin
steps.stepSummary: Before he died, the חסיד said he knew his only sin was the goat, because he broke the ruling of the חכמים not to raise small animals in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: He himself also said when he was dying: I know that I have no sin except that goat alone, because I went against the words of my colleagues. The חכמים said: one may not raise small animals (sheep and goats) in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The man confirms on his deathbed what his friends found: the goat was his only sin. He also explains why it was a sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now two witnesses agree, his friends and the man himself. The sin was breaking a rabbinic rule against raising sheep and goats in ארץ ישראל. Apart from this one sin, he seems to be a sage with no flaw.

keyTerms.meaning: The words (rulings) of my colleagues, the חכמים

steps.confusionAlert: Keeping the goat was not breaking a Torah law. It went against a ruling of the חכמים. Even so, he himself counted it as a real sin, his only one.

phrases.english: And he himself also said at the time of his death:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹדֵעַ אֲנִי בְּעַצְמִי שֶׁאֵין בִּי עָוֹן,
phrases.english: I know about myself that I have no sin,
except the sin of that goat alone,
because I went against the words of my colleagues,
for the Sages said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְגַדְּלִין בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: one may not raise small animals in the Land of Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the man's own testimony to his friends' findings.
steps.raayaObject: That the goat was the man's only sin.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The man's own deathbed statement, together with the ruling of the חכמים against raising small animals.

steps.title: The pious man lived long after יוסף בן יועזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא applies a known rule: 'a certain חסיד' means רבי יהודה בן בבא or רבי יהודה בר אילעאי. Both lived many generations after יוסף בן יועזר, which contradicts step 23.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we have a rule: wherever it says 'a story with a certain pious man,' it means either רבי יהודה בן בבא or רבי יהודה בר אילעאי. And these sages lived many generations after יוסף בן יועזר of צרידה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge by identifying who the pious man was. He lived long after יוסף בן יועזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 23 said that after יוסף בן יועזר the sages had some flaw. But this חסיד lived generations later and had no sin except the goat. So the ברייתא in step 23 seems to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, we have an established rule
'A story with a certain pious man,' a fixed phrase that points to a specific sage

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge: a sage from much later than יוסף בן יועזר was flawless except for the goat. That seems to contradict the ברייתא that the sages after יוסף בן יועזר had a flaw.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that 'a certain חסיד' means one of two specific sages is a useful key for reading many stories across the תלמוד.

phrases.english: And we have an established rule,
anywhere it says 'an incident with a certain pious man' —
it is either Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava
or Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן בָּתַר יוֹסֵף בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
phrases.english: and these Sages, after Yosef ben Yo'ezer of Tzereida,
lived many generations later.
phrases.notes: The point is left unsaid: so there were flawless sages even after יוסף בן יועזר, against step 23.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקַיְימָא לַן, כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּאָמַר מַעֲשֶׂה בְּחָסִיד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the חסיד and his time period, which turns the story into a direct challenge to step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא in step 23 that the אשכולות after יוסף בן יועזר had a flaw.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חסיד was רבי יהודה בן בבא or רבי יהודה בר אילעאי, who lived generations after יוסף בן יועזר. He had no sin except the goat, so flawless sages existed after יוסף בן יועזר.
